title: Star trails at La Silla
caption: Star trails over the Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope, La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: This night shot at ESO's La Silla Observatory shows the Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope, known as SEST, with the ESO 3.6-metre telescope in the background. ESO titled the picture 'Star trails at La Silla', and the trails of stars sweep across the sky above the two instruments.
Star trails appear when a camera gathers light over a long period while the Earth turns. The stars seem to wheel across the sky, and the camera records that motion as streaks instead of points.

The two telescopes are very different. SEST, as its name says, was built to observe submillimetre light, a kind of radiation well beyond what our eyes can detect. ESO Photo Ambassador Yuri Beletsky took the photograph as part of the ESO Ultra High Definition Expedition.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph at ESO's La Silla Observatory, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points. Only a long exposure turns the Earth's rotation into visible trails.
